# Independently authored text preparation cases

These ASCII DXF files were hand-authored for the Text/MText implementation on
2026-10-06. They are not generated by either native converter and are not
AutoCAD-authored interoperability or rendering evidence. Expected values in
`cases.json` were derived from the literal fields and simple independent
arithmetic, not from the implementation under test.

Both files declare AC1032 (R2018) and millimetres (`$INSUNITS = 4`). They use
explicit local STYLE entries `Labels` and `Unused`. Unused styles are authored
data, not reader-synthesized defaults. Font names are symbolic requests; no font
file is required, loaded or supplied. Entity handles identify fixture records
only and are never native identity expectations.

## TEXT anchors and OCS

`text-layouts.dxf` exercises the four native layout families. Left/baseline uses
group 10; other ordinary alignments and whole-text-middle use group 11. Inactive
points in the first four cases are deliberately different. They are not a
second native anchor or editing history.

For the aligned case, endpoints (0,0,0) and (3,4,0) give length 5 and direction
(3/5,4/5,0). The stored source height is redundant for the native Aligned layout.
For Fit, endpoints (5,6,7) and (13,6,7) give length 8 at elevation 7 and preserve
nominal height 2.5.

The tilted TEXT normal is +Y. The arbitrary-axis construction independently
gives X=(-1,0,0), Y=(0,0,1), normal=(0,1,0). OCS insertion (3,4,5) therefore maps
to scope anchor (-3,5,4). A separate generation-bits case uses bits 2 and 4 to
exercise backward and upside-down mirrors without reversing the string.

## MTEXT structure and WCS

`mtext-markup.dxf` includes a WCS insertion (100,50,7), direction +Y and normal
+Z. The corresponding native direction basis can be X=(0,1,0), Y=(-1,0,0),
with separate native rotation zero. The insertion is never transformed as TEXT
OCS. Attachment and paragraph alignment are independent.

The first MTEXT value begins/ends with `\P`, has a second consecutive paragraph
break, uses `^I` as a lexical tab, and a horizontal stack. Its paragraph
breaks are explicit authored data; no automatic wrapping is stored.
Another value uses scoped underline and cumulative relative heights 0.2x and
1.25x; the nominal-height factors are 0.2 and 0.25, with restoration after the
closing brace. Literal escapes protect backslash, braces and field-like syntax.

Production source-reader characterization: the pinned ASCII stream reader
replaces `^I` with an actual TAB before `CadDocument` is exposed. The fixture
test therefore compares the decoded tab meaning, not that lexical spelling.
The standalone grammar retains the two spellings when operating directly on
source strings. Neither behavior proves preservation of `^J` line-break
semantics or of literal caret sequences through file writing.

Decimal markers, paragraph spacing units, dynamic-column zero sentinels,
independent MTEXT mirrors, vertical glyph metrics and actual font extents are
**not qualified** by these fixtures. Their native-only/known-restriction cases
in the index make that boundary explicit. No selected DXF sample is an import
allow-list. Production CAD and both native readers must still qualify the
exchange profiles in C1.
